title: Regular Weyl systems, projective symmetry and massive particles

items.title: Finite canonical representation interface
items.statement: Assuming AC, a nonzero irreducible regular Weyl system on a finite-dimensional real symplectic space with fixed nonzero central parameter is unitarily equivalent to the Schrödinger system; regularity, finite phase space, irreducibility, and the nonzero parameter are necessary hypotheses.
items.proof_route: Apply the current imported finite-dimensional Stone–von Neumann theorem with its actual AC, finite-phase-space, regularity, irreducibility, and nonzero-parameter hypotheses; compose intertwiners for uniqueness.

items.title: Mass cocycle for translations and boosts
items.statement: On L²(R^d), T(a)f(x)=f(x−a) and B_m(v)f(x)=e^(imv·x/ℏ)f(x) obey B_m(v)T(a)=e^(imv·a/ℏ)T(a)B_m(v). The group law (a,v,θ)(a',v',θ')=(a+a',v+v',θ+θ'−v'·a) defines a central extension, represented by the strongly continuous unitary representation Π_m(a,v,θ)=e^(imθ/ℏ)B_m(v)T(a); distinct positive masses give distinct central characters χ_m(θ)=e^(imθ/ℏ). The canonical Schrödinger Weyl system is regular and irreducible; fixed-parameter irreducible regular Weyl systems are unitarily equivalent.
items.proof_route: Prove translations and modulations unitary, derive their exact commutator and central-extension group law, establish strong continuity on a dense smooth core and extend by unitarity, distinguish central characters, then apply finite Weyl uniqueness.

items.title: Spin rotations and projective SO(3)
items.statement: For a differentiable finite-dimensional spin-s irreducible unitary SU(2) representation, D(−I)=(−1)^(2s)I. Its ray action descends to SO(3); integer spin descends as an ordinary unitary representation, while half-integer spin descends only projectively.
items.proof_route: Identify the 2π z-rotation with −I, exponentiate its finite self-adjoint generator, evaluate on the spin-s weight basis supplied by the current finite spin-block theorem, then descend through the two-sheeted cover.

items.title: Sector restriction as observable algebra
items.statement: For H=⊕_(j=1)^r H_j and the bounded block-diagonal algebra A=⊕_j B(H_j), every trace-class ρ satisfies tr(ρA)=tr((∑_j P_jρP_j)A) for all A∈A. Off-diagonal coherence is invisible only relative to this declared algebra.
items.proof_route: Expand the trace over the finitely many orthogonal blocks and use the published bounded-cyclicity lemma to make every off-diagonal block trace vanish; this is algebra-relative, not a universal superselection claim.

title: Regular Weyl systems, projective symmetry and massive particles — Examples

items.title: Boost-translation loop phase
items.statement: The loop B_m(v)T(a)B_m(v)*T(a)* equals e^(imv·a/ℏ)I; a relative phase changes the squared overlap only in an explicitly controlled two-arm path model.
items.proof_route: Use the exact cocycle for the loop; define a two-dimensional arm space and one-arm phase gate, then compute the output overlap and compare it with a common global phase.

items.title: Finite matrices cannot satisfy exact canonical commutation relations
items.statement: There are no finite d×d complex matrices Q,P with [Q,P]=iℏI_d for d≥1 and ℏ>0, since tr[Q,P]=0 but tr(iℏI_d)=iℏd.
items.proof_route: Define the finite matrix trace and expand tr(QP) and tr(PQ) as finite sums; reindex one sum and use commutativity of complex multiplication to get a contradiction.
